across.es: en todo; a lo largo de

activity.en: things people do, here private medical work
activity.ex: There is a lot of activity in the market today.

affected.ex: The storm affected many homes near the river.

agreed.ex: My parents agreed to let me travel alone.

aim.ex: The new school aims to help every child read.

allowed.ex: The teacher allowed us to leave early.

almost.ex: It is almost time for dinner.

alone.ex: Money alone cannot make you happy.

anticipates.ex: We anticipate heavy traffic on Friday evening.

argued.en: gave reasons to say something is true
argued.ex: She argued that the plan was too expensive.

arrangements.en: plans or agreements about how things work
arrangements.ex: We made arrangements to meet at the station.

ask.en: to say you want someone to do something
ask.ex: Please ask him to call me back.

asked.en: said a question to get an answer
asked.ex: She asked me where the bank was.

assurances.en: promises that something is true or will happen
assurances.ex: He gave assurances that the work would finish soon.

attention.ex: The new film got a lot of attention.

attracted.en: caused people to notice or come
attracted.ex: The festival attracted thousands of visitors.

baby.ex: The baby is sleeping in her room.

backed.en: back down: stopped arguing and accepted
backed.ex: He backed down after his boss said no.

bans.en: officially says something is not allowed
bans.ex: The city bans cars from the old town.

be.en: to exist or have a quality

bear.en: to suffer or carry something hard
bear.ex: Poor families bear the cost of high prices.

became.ex: The small shop became very popular.

being.en: used in passive forms in progress

board.en: group of people who manage an organisation
board.ex: The school board will meet on Monday.

broke.ex: He broke the law by driving too fast.

broken.ex: She has never broken a promise to me.

brunt.en: the worst part of something bad
brunt.ex: Small farms took the brunt of the dry weather.
brunt.zh: bear the brunt：首當其衝；承受最大衝擊

build.en: to make or create something over time
build.ex: They want to build a better future for children.

came.en: past of 'come'; moved into a state
came.ex: The truth came to light years later.
came.zh: come into conflict / come to light：陷入衝突／曝光

cannot.en: are not able or allowed to
cannot.ex: You cannot park here after six.

care.ex: My grandmother needs care at home.

carried.ex: The test was carried out last week.

carroll.en: part of the minister's family name

ceased.ex: The noise suddenly ceased at midnight.

cent.en: per cent: out of every hundred
cent.ex: Ten per cent of the students are absent.

central.ex: Family is central to her life.

certain.ex: Certain shops close early on Sundays.

change.ex: The change in weather surprised everyone.

check.en: a look to make sure something is right
check.ex: The doctor did a quick check of my heart.

checked.en: looked at something to see if it is right
checked.ex: I checked my answers before giving the test.

choice.ex: You have a choice of tea or coffee.

clarification.en: an explanation that makes something clear
clarification.ex: I need clarification about the new rules.

clashed.en: argued strongly or fought with someone
clashed.ex: The two leaders clashed over taxes.

clause.en: one part of a legal agreement
clause.ex: Read every clause before signing the contract.

come.ex: All good things come to an end.

companies.en: businesses that sell goods or services
companies.ex: Many companies let staff work from home.

compliance.ex: Compliance with safety rules is checked every month.
compliance.ja: 遵守；コンプライアンス

example.en: The company must ensure compliance with safety laws.
example.zh: 公司必須確保遵守安全法規。

note.meaning: 遵守規定、法律或合約要求的狀態。
note.usage: 常用 compliance with + 規則；反義為 non-compliance。多見於法律、商業與政策文章。

noteEn.meaning: the act of obeying a rule, law or agreement.
noteEn.usage: Use 'compliance with' + a rule; the opposite is 'non-compliance'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa debe garantizar el cumplimiento de las leyes de seguridad.
noteEs.meaning: cumplimiento de normas, leyes o contratos.
noteEs.usage: Se usa compliance with + norma; lo contrario es non-compliance.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी को सुरक्षा क़ानूनों का पालन सुनिश्चित करना होगा।
noteHi.meaning: नियमों, क़ानून या अनुबंध का पालन करना।
noteHi.usage: compliance with + नियम; उल्टा non-compliance। औपचारिक लेखन में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 会社は安全法の遵守を確保しなければならない。
noteJa.meaning: 規則・法律・契約を守ること。
noteJa.usage: compliance with＋規則 の形が多い。反対語は non-compliance。

noteKo.usage: compliance with + 규칙 형태로 자주 쓴다. 반대말은 non-compliance.

component.en: one part of a bigger system
component.ex: Trust is a key component of any team.

conceded.ex: The company conceded and raised the workers' pay.

example.en: After a long debate, the council conceded.
example.zh: 經過長時間辯論後，議會讓步了。

note.meaning: （在爭執中）讓步、認輸；勉強承認。
note.usage: 可接 that 子句（concede that…）或受詞（concede defeat）；語氣正式。

noteEn.meaning: to stop fighting or arguing and accept the other side.
noteEn.usage: Use 'concede that...' or 'concede defeat'; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: Tras un largo debate, el consejo cedió.
noteEs.meaning: ceder o reconocer la derrota en una disputa.
noteEs.usage: Se usa concede that... o concede defeat; es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: लंबी बहस के बाद परिषद झुक गई।
noteHi.meaning: बहस में हार मानना या झुक जाना।
noteHi.usage: concede that... या concede defeat; औपचारिक प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 長い議論の末、議会は譲歩した。
noteJa.meaning: 争いで譲歩する；しぶしぶ認める。
noteJa.usage: concede that… や concede defeat の形。改まった語。

noteKo.usage: concede that... 또는 concede defeat로 쓴다. 격식체.

concluded.en: decided something after thinking or studying
concluded.ex: The study concluded that sleep helps memory.

conducted.ex: The police conducted a search of the house.

conflict.ex: The conflict between the neighbours lasted years.

consequently.ex: It rained; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerably.ex: Prices have risen considerably this year.

consistent.ex: His story is consistent with the facts.

constituted.ex: This decision constituted a big change in policy.

example.en: Women constitute half of the workforce.

note.meaning: 構成；等同於、算是（某事物）。
note.usage: 正式用語，相當於 be 或 form；常用 constitute a + 名詞（如 constitute a threat）。

noteEn.meaning: to form something, or to be the same as something.
noteEn.usage: A formal way to say 'be' or 'form'; often 'constitute a' + noun.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las mujeres constituyen la mitad de la plantilla.
noteEs.usage: Forma formal de be o form; constitute a + sustantivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: महिलाएँ कार्यबल का आधा हिस्सा हैं।
noteHi.meaning: बनाना; किसी चीज़ के बराबर होना।
noteHi.usage: be या form का औपचारिक रूप; constitute a + संज्ञा।

noteJa.exampleTr: 女性が労働力の半分を占めている。
noteJa.usage: be や form の改まった言い方。constitute a＋名詞 が多い。

noteKo.usage: be나 form의 격식체. constitute a + 명사 형태가 많다.

consultant.ex: The consultant explained the results of my scan.

consultants.en: senior hospital doctors who are specialists
consultants.ex: Two consultants checked the patient this morning.

contingent.ex: The trip is contingent on good weather.

example.en: The job offer is contingent on a health check.
example.zh: 這份工作錄取要以通過健康檢查為條件。

note.meaning: 取決於某條件；要等某事發生才成立。
note.usage: 固定搭配 contingent on/upon + 名詞，語氣正式，常見於合約與政策。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'contingent on' or 'contingent upon' + noun; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: La oferta de trabajo depende de un examen médico.
noteEs.usage: Se usa contingent on/upon + sustantivo; es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: नौकरी का प्रस्ताव स्वास्थ्य जाँच पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.usage: contingent on/upon + संज्ञा; औपचारिक प्रयोग, अनुबंधों में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: その採用は健康診断が条件となっている。
noteJa.usage: contingent on/upon＋名詞 の形で使う。改まった表現。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 일자리 제안은 건강 검진 통과가 조건이다.
noteKo.usage: contingent on/upon + 명사 형태로 쓰며 격식체이다.

continuing.ex: She is continuing her studies abroad.

contract.en: a legal written agreement about work
contract.ex: He signed a two-year contract with the club.

contracts.ex: All workers must sign new contracts.

cornerstone.ex: Trust is the cornerstone of a good friendship.

cost.en: money or loss needed for something
cost.ex: The cost of living keeps going up.

cover.ex: Does your policy give cover for theft?

deliver.en: to provide or achieve what was promised
deliver.ex: The new team must deliver better results.

democrats.en: part of the party name Social Democrats
democrats.zh: Social Democrats：社會民主黨（愛爾蘭政黨）

derived.ex: Many towns derive income from tourism.

example.en: The island derives most of its income from tourism.
example.zh: 這座島的大部分收入來自旅遊業。

note.meaning: 從某來源取得（收入、好處等）；源自。
note.usage: 常用 derive A from B；被動 be derived from 也很常見。

noteEn.meaning: to get something from a particular source.
noteEn.usage: Use 'derive A from B'; the passive 'be derived from' is common.

noteEs.exampleTr: La isla obtiene la mayor parte de sus ingresos del turismo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa derive A from B; también be derived from.

noteHi.exampleTr: द्वीप अपनी अधिकतर आय पर्यटन से प्राप्त करता है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी स्रोत से कुछ प्राप्त करना।
noteHi.usage: derive A from B; passive be derived from भी आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: その島は収入の大半を観光から得ている。
noteJa.meaning: ある源から何かを得る。
noteJa.usage: derive A from B の形。受動態 be derived from もよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 섬은 수입의 대부분을 관광에서 얻는다.
noteKo.usage: derive A from B 형태. 수동태 be derived from도 많다.

described.ex: The hotel was described as clean and quiet.

discontinued.ex: This phone model was discontinued last year.

example.en: The bus route was discontinued last year.
example.zh: 這條公車路線去年停駛了。

note.meaning: 正式停止、終止某項服務、產品或做法。
note.usage: 常用被動 be discontinued；比 stop 正式，多用於官方或商業語境。

noteEn.meaning: to officially stop doing or providing something.
noteEn.usage: Often passive: 'be discontinued'; more formal than 'stop'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La línea de autobús se suprimió el año pasado.
noteEs.meaning: suspender o dejar de ofrecer algo oficialmente.
noteEs.usage: Frecuente en pasiva: be discontinued; más formal que stop.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह बस मार्ग पिछले साल बंद कर दिया गया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी सेवा या काम को आधिकारिक रूप से बंद करना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर passive: be discontinued; stop से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのバス路線は昨年廃止された。
noteJa.meaning: サービスや慣行を正式にやめる。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be discontinued が多い。stop より改まった語。

noteKo.usage: 수동태 be discontinued로 자주 쓴다. stop보다 격식 있다.

disproportionately.en: much more than is fair or normal
disproportionately.ex: Older people are disproportionately affected by the heat.

example.en: Young workers were disproportionately affected by job cuts.
example.zh: 年輕員工受裁員的影響格外嚴重。

note.meaning: 不成比例地；某群體受影響的程度明顯大於其他群體。
note.usage: 常修飾 affected、hit、high 等，如 be disproportionately affected。

noteEn.meaning: much more than is fair or usual compared to others.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los trabajadores jóvenes se vieron desproporcionadamente afectados por los despidos.
noteEs.meaning: de forma desproporcionada, mucho más que otros.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir con affected, hit, high: be disproportionately affected.

noteHi.exampleTr: नौकरी कटौती से युवा कर्मचारी असमान रूप से अधिक प्रभावित हुए।
noteHi.meaning: अनुपात से अधिक; दूसरों की तुलना में बहुत ज़्यादा।
noteHi.usage: affected, hit, high के साथ: be disproportionately affected।

noteJa.exampleTr: 若い労働者は人員削減の影響を不釣り合いに大きく受けた。
noteJa.meaning: 不釣り合いに；他より大きく。
noteJa.usage: affected, hit, high などを修飾。be disproportionately affected が典型。

noteKo.exampleTr: 젊은 노동자들이 감원의 영향을 불균형적으로 크게 받았다.
noteKo.usage: affected, hit, high 등을 수식한다. be disproportionately affected가 대표적.

disproportionately.zh: 不成比例地；格外嚴重地

down.en: back down: give up a position
down.ex: She would not back down in the argument.

drying.en: dry up: slowly stop coming or existing
drying.ex: Money for the project is drying up.

effect.en: to that effect: with that meaning
effect.ex: She said something to that effect.
effect.zh: to that effect：大意如此；意思相同

end.ex: The film had a happy end.
end.zh: come to an end：結束；in the end：最後

ended.ex: The meeting ended at five o'clock.

enforced.en: made sure people obey a rule
enforced.ex: The new speed limit will be strictly enforced.

enough.ex: We have enough food for everyone.

establish.en: to start or create something lasting
establish.ex: They plan to establish a new school here.

even.en: even though: despite the fact that
even.ex: He went out even though it was cold.

eventually.en: in the end, after a long time
eventually.ex: He eventually found a job he liked.

exchange.en: in exchange for: giving one thing to get another
exchange.ex: I helped him in exchange for a meal.

executive.en: part of the name of Ireland's health agency
executive.ex: The executive will announce the plan tomorrow.
executive.zh: Health Service Executive：（愛爾蘭）衛生服務署

exercise.en: an activity done for a specific purpose
exercise.ex: The survey was a useful exercise for the team.

expensive.ex: This restaurant is too expensive for us.

faced.ex: Faced with rain, we stayed inside.

facilities.en: buildings or places for a purpose
facilities.ex: The school has good sports facilities.

fee-paying.ex: Fee-paying schools can be very expensive.

fifth.ex: A fifth of the class was sick.

first.ex: This is my first visit to Japan.

flagged.en: marked as a problem needing attention
flagged.ex: The bank flagged the payment as unusual.

focusing.en: giving most attention to one thing
focusing.ex: She is focusing on her exams this month.

follow.ex: Please follow the rules in the library.

followed.ex: The children followed the teacher's instructions.

follows.ex: Every player follows the same rules.

for.en: used to show purpose or who gets something

formal.ex: You will get a formal letter next week.

found.ex: The study found that children need more sleep.

fundamental.ex: Clean water is a fundamental need.

funding.ex: The school lost its government funding.

generous.ex: She got a generous gift from her uncle.

get.ex: You get a free drink with every meal.

give.en: to hand over; give up: stop having
give.ex: Can you give me your phone number?

given.ex: She has given me a lot of help.

go.en: move or pass to a place

good.ex: This is a good book for beginners.

hardest.ex: Poor families were hit hardest by the price rise.

health.en: the state of the body; medical services
health.ex: Exercise is good for your health.

healthcare.en: medical services to keep people healthy
healthcare.ex: Everyone should have access to healthcare.

hit.ex: The town was hit by floods.

holding.ex: People holding tickets can enter now.

horns.en: lock horns: argue strongly with someone
horns.ex: The two managers often lock horns over money.
horns.zh: lock horns：激烈爭執；正面交鋒

hospital.en: a place where sick people get treatment
hospital.ex: She works at the local hospital.

hospital's.ex: The hospital's car park is full.

hospitals.en: places where sick people get treatment
hospitals.ex: The city has three big hospitals.

how.ex: Can you show me how this machine works?

hse.ja: HSE（アイルランド保健サービス庁）

hse's.en: belonging to the Health Service Executive

human.ex: She works in human resources at a bank.

identified.ex: The police identified the driver from a photo.

implementation.en: the process of putting a plan into action
implementation.ex: The implementation of the new law took two years.

example.en: The implementation of the plan will take a year.
example.zh: 這項計畫的實施需要一年時間。

note.meaning: 把計畫、政策或制度付諸實行的過程。
note.usage: 常用 the implementation of + 計畫/政策；動詞為 implement。

noteEn.meaning: the process of putting a plan or policy into action.
noteEn.usage: Use 'the implementation of' + plan; the verb is 'implement'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La implementación del plan llevará un año.
noteEs.meaning: proceso de poner en práctica un plan o política.
noteEs.usage: Se usa the implementation of + plan; el verbo es implement.

noteHi.exampleTr: योजना को लागू करने में एक साल लगेगा।
noteHi.meaning: योजना या नीति को लागू करने की प्रक्रिया।
noteHi.usage: the implementation of + नीति; क्रिया implement।

noteJa.exampleTr: その計画の実施には1年かかる。
noteJa.meaning: 計画や政策を実行に移すこと。
noteJa.usage: the implementation of＋計画 の形。動詞は implement。

noteKo.usage: the implementation of + 계획 형태. 동사는 implement.

implemented.ex: The new system will be implemented next month.

implications.ex: The decision has serious implications for jobs.

important.ex: Sleep is important for your health.

income.ex: Their income went up this year.

indemnity.en: insurance that pays if you are blamed
indemnity.ex: Doctors need indemnity in case of mistakes.

indicated.ex: He indicated that he would accept the job.

initial.ex: My initial idea was to take a train.

insufficient.ex: There was insufficient evidence to prove it.

insurance.en: paying money so you are protected from costs

insurers.ex: Insurers raised prices after the floods.

intended.ex: This book is intended for young readers.

into.en: moving to the inside or a state

introduced.en: started or brought in for the first time
introduced.ex: The school introduced a new uniform.

issue.en: a problem or subject people discuss
issue.ex: Housing is a big issue in the city.

jennifer.en: first name of the Health Minister

keeping.en: in keeping with: matching or suitable for
keeping.ex: The new house is in keeping with the old street.

know.ex: I want to know the truth.

known.en: known as: called by a name
known.ex: The city is known as the Big Apple.

largely.ex: The book is largely about his childhood.

leave.en: to cause something to be in a state
leave.ex: The storm will leave many homes without power.

legacy.en: left over from an older system
legacy.ex: The bank still uses legacy computer systems.

light.ex: New facts came to light during the trial.

locked.ex: The two teams locked horns in the final.

longer.ex: He no longer lives in London.

looked.ex: The teacher looked at my homework.

losing.ex: He is afraid of losing his job.

loss.en: having less of something than before
loss.ex: The company reported a loss this year.

macneill.en: part of the minister's family name

mainly.ex: The class is mainly for beginners.

mairéad.en: first name of an HSE official

make.en: make sure: check that something happens
make.ex: Make sure you lock the door.

maternity.ex: She works in the maternity ward.

matter.ex: We need to discuss this matter today.

measures.en: actions taken to deal with a problem
measures.ex: The government took measures to cut pollution.

minister.en: a leader of a government department
minister.ex: The minister visited the new school.

money.en: what you use to buy things
money.ex: We need more money for the trip.

mostly.ex: The students are mostly from Spain.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

non-compliant.ex: The factory was fined for non-compliant waste disposal.

office.ex: Her office is on the third floor.

old.ex: I still have my old phone.

or.en: used to show another name or choice

out.en: part of phrasal verbs like 'carry out'
out.ex: They carried out the plan quickly.
out.zh: carry out / spell out / roll out 片語用字

paid.ex: The bill was paid by my father.

part.ex: This is the best part of the film.

particular.ex: Pay particular attention to the last question.

patients.ex: The doctor sees twenty patients a day.

pay.ex: The pay in this job is good.

plan.en: a set of ideas for doing something
plan.ex: We have a plan for the weekend.

pocc.zh: 公立專職顧問醫師合約（POCC）

practice.en: the work of a doctor; put into practice: do
practice.ex: She opened a private practice in the city.

predominantly.ex: The town is predominantly young families.

preliminary.en: coming first, before the main part

premises.en: the building and land of a business
premises.ex: No smoking is allowed on the premises.

pressing.en: strongly asking someone to do something
pressing.ex: Parents are pressing the school for smaller classes.

previous.ex: The previous owner left the house clean.

previously.ex: She previously worked as a teacher.

private.en: paid for by people, not the state
private.ex: He goes to a private school.

problem.ex: We have a problem with the car.

programme.ex: The government started a new health programme.

prohibiting.ex: There is a sign prohibiting dogs in the park.

prohibits.ex: The law prohibits selling alcohol to children.

projects.en: calculates what will happen in future
projects.ex: The bank projects slow growth next year.

promises.en: statements that you will do something
promises.ex: Politicians often make promises before elections.

prospect.en: the chance that something will happen
prospect.ex: The prospect of losing his job worried him.

provided.ex: The school provided lunch for all students.

provisions.en: rules or conditions in a legal document
provisions.ex: The law has special provisions for older workers.

example.en: The contract includes provisions for sick leave.
example.zh: 這份合約包含病假的相關條款。

note.meaning: 法律、合約或協議中的條款或規定。
note.usage: 此義多用複數 provisions；常說 under the provisions of…。另有「提供」之義。

noteEn.meaning: a rule or condition in a law or contract.
noteEn.usage: Usually plural 'provisions'; 'under the provisions of' is common.

noteEs.exampleTr: El contrato incluye disposiciones sobre la baja por enfermedad.
noteEs.meaning: disposición o cláusula de una ley o contrato.
noteEs.usage: En este sentido suele ir en plural: provisions; under the provisions of...

noteHi.exampleTr: अनुबंध में बीमारी की छुट्टी के प्रावधान शामिल हैं।
noteHi.meaning: क़ानून या अनुबंध की कोई शर्त या नियम।
noteHi.usage: इस अर्थ में अक्सर बहुवचन provisions; under the provisions of...।

paragraphs: Senior hospital doctors in Ireland have stopped seeing private patients in public hospitals. A new report from the HSE says this.
The HSE runs the public health service. It checked a new contract for these doctors. The contract says they can only treat public patients in public hospitals.

In the summer, there was a problem at the Rotunda Hospital in Dublin. Some doctors there still saw private patients. The Health Minister, Jennifer Carroll MacNeill, said the hospital could lose money. The hospital then followed the rules.
The new contract started in 2023. Doctors get more pay. But they cannot take money from private patients in public hospitals.
There is a cost. Hospitals will lose almost €145 million. Women who want private care when they have a baby will slowly lose that choice.

A new review by the Health Service Executive (HSE) says that senior hospital doctors, called consultants, have stopped treating private patients in public hospitals. This is what their new contracts ask them to do.

The review was a first check on the Public-Only Consultants Contract, or POCC. It looked mainly at one rule: consultants on this contract must not do private work in public hospitals. Mairéad Ryan, who works in the HSE's human resources office, said all the arrangements that broke the rules had ended. Every health region told the HSE that private work had stopped.

The problem became public in the summer. Some consultants at the Rotunda Hospital in Dublin were still seeing private patients, even though they had public-only contracts. The Minister for Health, Jennifer Carroll MacNeill, said the hospital could lose its funding and insurance cover. In the end, the hospital board agreed to follow the rules.
Pádraig Rice, health spokesperson for the Social Democrats, said promises were not enough. He wants to know how the HSE will make sure every public hospital follows the contract.

The POCC started in 2023. It is an important part of Sláintecare, a plan to give everyone in Ireland good public healthcare. Consultants on the contract get higher pay. In return, they cannot treat paying patients in public hospitals. Under the old contract, up to 20 per cent of their work could be private.

But the change is expensive. Money from private patients, mostly paid by health insurance companies, used to go to hospitals. The HSE says hospitals will now be almost €145 million short. Maternity care is hit hardest, because Ireland has no private maternity hospitals.

The review was a first check on how the Public-Only Consultants Contract, known as the POCC, is being put into practice. It looked in particular at the clause that bans private work in public settings. Mairéad Ryan, from the HSE's national human resources office, said arrangements that had broken the rules had ended, and every health region had given assurances that private practice had stopped.

The issue came to light in the summer, when the Minister for Health, Jennifer Carroll MacNeill, clashed with the board of the Rotunda Hospital in Dublin. Some consultants there were still seeing private patients while on public-only contracts. The minister threatened the hospital's funding and insurance cover, and the board eventually backed down.
The Social Democrats' health spokesperson, Pádraig Rice, said assurances were not enough. He asked what steps were being taken to make sure every public hospital follows the contract.

The POCC was introduced in 2023 as a central part of Sláintecare, the plan to build a universal health service. Consultants on the contract earn higher salaries but give up the right to treat fee-paying patients in public hospitals. Under the old contract, up to 20 per cent of their work could be private.

The change has a cost. The HSE says the loss of private income, mostly from health insurers, will leave hospitals almost €145 million short. Maternity care is especially affected, because Ireland has no private maternity hospitals.

Private practice by consultants within public hospitals has come to an end, according to a review carried out by the Health Service Executive (HSE), which says the shift is in keeping with the terms of their new contracts.

The review, described as a preliminary verification exercise, scrutinised how the Public-Only Consultants Contract (POCC) is being rolled out, with particular attention to the clause prohibiting private work on public premises. Mairéad Ryan of the HSE's national human resources office stated that arrangements previously flagged as non-compliant had been wound up, and that every region had provided assurances to that effect.

The matter surfaced over the summer, when the Minister for Health, Jennifer Carroll MacNeill, locked horns with the board of the Rotunda Hospital in Dublin, where some consultants on public-only terms were still treating private patients. Faced with the prospect of losing its funding and indemnity cover, the board ultimately backed down.

The Social Democrats' health spokesperson, Pádraig Rice, has demanded more than reassurances, pressing the HSE to spell out how compliance will be enforced across every public hospital so that legacy arrangements cannot stall reform.

Introduced in 2023 as a cornerstone of the Sláintecare reforms, which aim to deliver universal healthcare, the POCC offers consultants more generous salaries in exchange for surrendering the right to treat fee-paying patients in public facilities. The previous contract permitted up to a fifth of their workload to be private.

The reform is not without cost. With private income, largely paid by health insurers, drying up, the HSE anticipates a shortfall of almost €145 million for hospitals. Maternity services bear the brunt, since the State has no private maternity hospitals.
